claims.text: Rapid solidification produces a non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with an initially homogeneous, metastable Mg-rich solid solution.
The initial solid solution contains dispersed, unstable intermetallic clusters.
Controlled thermal aging or high-temperature environmental exposure induces diffusional segregation of Mg from the supersaturated matrix.
Thermal evolution transforms the metastable solid solution into stable intermetallic phases.
Temperatures between 600°C and 900°C provide sufficient diffusion for the proposed transformation.
Stable intermetallic precipitates form and grow both at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
The stable intermetallic precipitates are typically Mg-depleted.
The stable intermetallic precipitates are enriched in elements that promote passivation.
Formation of the stable intermetallic phases diminishes local micro-galvanic coupling.
The intermetallic phases provide nucleation sites that improve the adhesion and continuity of a protective oxide scale.
The cited Mg-rich alloy work associates processing and composition with intermetallic phases, passive-film formation, and corrosion resistance.
Relative to the unaged as-cast state, the aged alloy will have a lower corrosion current density.
Relative to the unaged as-cast state, the aged alloy will have a higher corrosion potential.
Relative to the unaged as-cast state, the aged alloy will show lower high-temperature oxidation mass gain.
Relative to the unaged as-cast state, the aged alloy will form a more adherent oxide scale.
The proposed mechanism is limited to rapidly solidified Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys that begin in a metastable state.
The proposed effect may be absent when the composition or processing conditions already produce stable phases.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as homogeneous while also containing dispersed intermetallic clusters. Unless 'homogeneous' is explicitly restricted to a larger length scale, the clusters imply structural or chemical heterogeneity.
